work with people who struggle to access services, I now see why this is an issue when I called to maked an appointment for a client this morning.
Firstly, I waited 20 minutes just to get put in a queue, then once the call was answered, I was asked what the issue was with client. I started to explain that he was experiencing sore throat, runny nose and chest pain. I was immediately cut of in my sentence and told he would need to access A&E for chest pain. I then tried to explain that he had this for 3 days and that it is worse for night time breathing....." you need to go A&E,ok' I then stated that I had not finished, the receptionist Hamera, continued to talk over me to the point where I felt it necessary to speak to the practice manger, what a mistake that was as she was completely unprofessional in in her manner, she started with her name and immediately stated that he would have to go to A&E. I then asked my client to explain why he wanted to see the GP, he started with saying he had a sore throat and was immediately cut off and told he needed to go to A&E as he already stated that he had chest pain. I then asked Jane if she was refusing to give my client an appointment, she stated that she was not refusing the appointment, but yet she then stated that he needs a pharmacy appointment as its not important enough to see theGP.
I found the whole conversation from start to finish completely unprofessional with a lack of respect being shown to my client. I continued to ask for a GP appointment and was then told there are no more appointments for today. I then asked if that was because I had been on the phone for 30 minutes talking to her ( Jane) about my client or is it because she did not want to admit I was right and that my client can call for a GP appointment if he feels its necessary, not because a receptionist or glorified receptionist with a title and no actual professional medical training can now decide who has a GP appointment and who doesn't. I was then told my client can go to ICT at 6.45pm this evening, I asked for a translator and was told she could not do that, I asked if it is not her remit to put a note on the system for a translator?  My client then explained to me that he gets this reaction every time he calls and feels that the staff are racist towards him.
The whole situation was dealt with very badly and I dread to think how staff respond to other people in my clients position with limited English and use a wrong word to describe how they feel.
